transcription.tex: Mechanics relates forces to motion. Draw the forces on each body separately, then use Newton’s second law, \(\sum\mathbf F=m\mathbf a\), to connect the resultant force to its acceleration.

shapes.alt: A particle on a table with weight down, reaction up, friction left and tension diagonally up and right.
Separate force arrows on connected 3 kg and 4 kg particles. The lighter mass accelerates up and the heavier down.
Displacement–time and velocity–time graphs. The shaded area under the velocity graph represents displacement.

transcription.tex: Weight \(mg\) acts down. The normal reaction \(R\) acts perpendicular to the table. Friction \(F\) opposes sliding or its tendency. Tension \(T\) acts along a taut string.\par In equilibrium the horizontal components balance and the vertical components balance. For connected particles, draw one force diagram per particle.
The gradient of a displacement–time graph is velocity. The gradient of a velocity–time graph is acceleration. Signed area under velocity–time gives displacement. Area under speed–time gives distance.

For constant acceleration \(a\), use displacement \(s\), initial velocity \(u\), final velocity \(v\) and time \(t\).\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\]\[v^2=u^2+2as,\quad s=\tfrac12(u+v)t.\]For variable acceleration use calculus. For example, \(s=2t^3+3t\) gives \(v=ds/dt=6t^2+3\), then \(a=dv/dt=12t\).

transcription.tex: A modelling assumption tells us which features of a real object to keep in a calculation. Identify the assumption that justifies each simplification.

shapes.alt: Particle in contact with a horizontal surface.

transcription.tex: A particle has negligible dimensions. Treat its mass as concentrated at a point and ignore rotation. Neglecting air resistance is a separate assumption. A smooth surface exerts no friction. A rough surface may exert friction.

shapes.alt: A single taut string connects two particles over a fixed pulley.

transcription.tex: A light, smooth pulley has negligible mass and no friction. In an ideal light string passing over it, tension is equal on either side. An inextensible string keeps its length. In this fixed-pulley system, the connected particles have equal acceleration magnitudes while the string is taut.

shapes.alt: A straight rigid rod resting on two fixed supports.

transcription.tex: A rod is rigid, with transverse dimensions negligible compared with its length. Model its mass along a line. A peg or support is fixed and its dimensions may be neglected. It can be smooth or rough as stated in the question.

transcription.tex: \[\begin{array}{lll}\text{Quantity}&\text{SI unit}&\text{Symbol}\\ \hline \text{Mass}&\text{kilogram}&\mathrm{kg}\\ \text{Length or displacement}&\text{metre}&\mathrm{m}\\ \text{Time}&\text{second}&\mathrm{s}\\ \text{Speed or velocity}&\text{metre per second}&\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\\ \text{Acceleration}&\text{metre per second squared}&\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\\ \text{Force or weight}&\text{newton}&\mathrm N\end{array}\]

Newton’s second law gives \[1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}.\] Convert measurements into compatible units before substituting into an equation. Mass is measured in kilograms; weight is a force measured in newtons.
The International System of Units (SI) lets us express measurements consistently. Use the table to check the units in a mechanics calculation.

transcription.tex: A scalar has magnitude only. A vector has magnitude and direction. Compare the length of the journey from \(A\) to \(B\) with its displacement.

shapes.alt: The same segment has length 5 metres. The arrow points 3 metres right and 4 metres up.

transcription.tex: The distance is \(5\,\mathrm m\). The displacement is \((3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\), with magnitude \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\,\mathrm m\). Speed is the magnitude of velocity. Force and acceleration are vectors, while time and mass are scalars.
A particle moves 3 m opposite to the chosen positive direction. State its distance travelled and displacement.

shapes.alt: Right is positive. A 3 m journey goes left from start to finish.

transcription.tex: Distance travelled is \(3\,\mathrm m\). Displacement is \(-3\,\mathrm m\). A signed number represents a vector along a chosen axis. The minus sign tells us which way the particle moved.

transcription.tex: 1. A displacement of magnitude \(5\,\mathrm m\) acts at \(60^\circ\) above the positive horizontal. Find its components.

shapes.alt: A displacement of magnitude \(5\,\mathrm m\) acts at \(60^\circ\) above the positive horizontal. Find its components.

transcription.tex: \(\mathbf s=(5\cos60^\circ)\mathbf i+(5\sin60^\circ)\mathbf j\).\par Thus \(\mathbf s=(2.5\mathbf i+4.33\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\) to 3 s.f.
2. The velocity is \((5\mathbf i-12\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the speed.

shapes.alt: The unit vectors i and j point to the right and upwards.

transcription.tex: Speed is the magnitude of velocity. Use Pythagoras:\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{5^2+(-12)^2}=\sqrt{169}=13\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]
3. A force of \(8\,\mathrm N\) acts at \(45^\circ\) below the positive horizontal. Find the force vector.

shapes.alt: A force of \(8\,\mathrm N\) acts at \(45^\circ\) below the positive horizontal. Find the force vector.

transcription.tex: Rightwards is positive, and downwards is negative.\[\mathbf F=8\cos45^\circ\,\mathbf i-8\sin45^\circ\,\mathbf j\]\[=(4\sqrt2\,\mathbf i-4\sqrt2\,\mathbf j)\,\mathrm N.\]
For a given angle, the adjacent component has magnitude \(R\cos\theta\) and the opposite component has magnitude \(R\sin\theta\). Choose each sign from the arrow direction.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: 1. A force of \(6\,\mathrm N\) acts down and left at \(60^\circ\) to the downward vertical. Find its components.

shapes.alt: A force of \(6\,\mathrm N\) acts down and left at \(60^\circ\) to the downward vertical. Find its components.

transcription.tex: The horizontal component is opposite the given angle and both components are negative.\[\mathbf F=-6\sin60^\circ\,\mathbf i-6\cos60^\circ\,\mathbf j\]\[=(-3\sqrt3\,\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm N.\]
2. An acceleration is \((6\mathbf i-8\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find its magnitude.

shapes.alt: The unit vectors i and j point to the right and upwards.

transcription.tex: The unit vectors \(\mathbf i,\mathbf j\) point right and up. The column of components is \(\binom{6}{-8}\).\[|\mathbf a|=\sqrt{6^2+(-8)^2}=\sqrt{100}=10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.\]
3. A displacement of \(4\,\mathrm m\) is directed \(30^\circ\) above the negative horizontal. Write it using unit vectors.

shapes.alt: A displacement of \(4\,\mathrm m\) is directed \(30^\circ\) above the negative horizontal. Write it using unit vectors.

transcription.tex: Leftwards is negative and upwards is positive.\[\mathbf s=-4\cos30^\circ\,\mathbf i+4\sin30^\circ\,\mathbf j\]\[=(-2\sqrt3\,\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m.\]
For a given angle, the adjacent component has magnitude \(R\cos\theta\) and the opposite component has magnitude \(R\sin\theta\). Choose each sign from the arrow direction.

transcription.tex: A man walks from \(A\) to \(B\) and then from \(B\) to \(C\). His displacement from \(A\) to \(B\) is \(6\mathbf i+4\mathbf j\) m. His displacement from \(B\) to \(C\) is \(5\mathbf i-12\mathbf j\) m.\par (a) What is the magnitude of the displacement from \(A\) to \(C\)?\par (b) What is the total distance the man has walked in getting from \(A\) to \(C\)?

shapes.alt: The man travels northeast from A to B, then southeast to C. The dashed arrow AC is the resultant.

transcription.tex: Add the displacement vectors:\[\overrightarrow{AC}=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}\]\[=(6+5)\mathbf i+(4-12)\mathbf j=11\mathbf i-8\mathbf j.\]Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{11^2+(-8)^2}=\sqrt{185}=13.6\,\mathrm m\) to 3 s.f.

Add the lengths of the two legs of the journey.\[AB=\sqrt{6^2+4^2}=\sqrt{52}\,\mathrm m,\quad BC=\sqrt{5^2+(-12)^2}=13\,\mathrm m.\]Total distance \(=\sqrt{52}+13\approx20.21\,\mathrm m\), or \(20.2\,\mathrm m\) to 3 s.f.

transcription.tex: Mr Bean’s car has a velocity of \(\binom{3}{-1}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Determine the angle the trajectory of the car makes with the unit vector \(\mathbf i\).

shapes.alt: A lime-green Mini with a black bonnet travelling to the right along a road.
The velocity triangle has horizontal component 3 to the right and vertical component 1 down. The angle lies below the positive horizontal.

transcription.tex: The horizontal component is \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and the downward component has magnitude \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).\[\tan\theta=\frac13,\qquad\theta=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac13\right)=18.4^\circ\ \text{(3 s.f.)}.\]The direction of travel is \(18.4^\circ\) below \(\mathbf i\).

transcription.tex: Question 2

The velocity of a car is given by \(\mathbf v=(12\mathbf i-10\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find: \par (a) the speed of the car \par (b) the angle the direction of motion of the car makes with the unit vector \(\mathbf i\).

\textbf{a} The perpendicular velocity components are \(12\) and \(-10\), in \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{12^2+(-10)^2}=\sqrt{244}=15.6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad\text{(3 s.f.)}.\]\par \textbf{b} The vector points right and down. The angle below \(\mathbf i\) satisfies \(\tan\theta=10/12\), so \(\theta=\tan^{-1}(10/12)=39.8^\circ\) to 3 s.f.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: Question 3

The acceleration of a motorbike is given by \(\mathbf a=3\mathbf i-4\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find: \par (a) the magnitude of the acceleration \par (b) the angle the direction of the acceleration vector makes with the unit vector \(\mathbf j\).

\textbf{a} Use Pythagoras on the components.\[|\mathbf a|=\sqrt{3^2+(-4)^2}=5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.\]\par \textbf{b} The vector points right and down. Its angle to the downward vertical is \(\tan^{-1}(3/4)=36.87^\circ\). The requested angle to the upward unit vector \(\mathbf j\) is \(180^\circ-36.87^\circ=143^\circ\) to 3 s.f.

transcription.tex: Question 7

The acceleration of a boat is given by \(\mathbf a=-0.05\mathbf i+0.15\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find: \par (a) the magnitude of the acceleration \par (b) the angle the direction of the acceleration vector makes with the unit vector \(\mathbf i\).

\textbf{a} The magnitude of the acceleration is \[\sqrt{(-0.05)^2+0.15^2}=\sqrt{0.025}=0.158\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\quad\text{(3 s.f.)}.\]\par \textbf{b} The vector points left and up. Its angle above the negative horizontal is \(\tan^{-1}(0.15/0.05)=\tan^{-1}3\). The angle from \(\mathbf i\) is \(180^\circ-\tan^{-1}3=108^\circ\) to 3 s.f.
